CAUTION

ADJACENT STRUCTURES AND DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(8) Do these steps to remove the sleeve [21]:
78-31-02
(a) Do these steps to re-tape the two upper and lower blocker doors:
NOTE: The upper and lower blocker doors overlap the fixed structure. The upper blocker
door must be taped so that it will stay partially open. No tape is necessary on the
lower blocker door. The remaining three blocker doors should be taped against
the wall.
1) Remove the tape from the upper and lower blocker doors.
2) Cut a new piece of speed tape approximately 15 in. (381 mm) long.
3) Put 5 in. (127 mm) of one end of the tape on the upper blocker door.
4) Put 5 in. (127 mm) of the other end of the tape on the outer wall of the fan duct.
5) Put another piece of speed tape perpendicular to and over the tape on the outer
wall of the fan duct.
(b) Manually push the sleeve aft approximately 15 in. (381 mm).
NOTE: If the sleeve is moved aft before the boom hoist is attached to the sling, there will
be less distance that the boom hoist has to be moved with it attached to the
sleeve. The boom hoist is easier to move before it is attached to the sleeve.
NOTE: The dimension that the sleeve extends aft to the completely extended position is
approximately 21.5 in. (546 mm).
(c) Do these steps to attach the sling assembly to the hoist (Figure 403):
NOTE: There are two boom hoists that can be used to carry out this task. The boom
hoist, SPL-1556, is applicable for the removal of the outboard sleeve only and
cannot be used for removal of the inboard sleeve. A suitable adapter is required
to attach the boom hoist, SPL-1556 to the sling [43].
NOTE: It is recommended to use boom hoist, SPL-2430.
1) If using boom hoist, SPL-1556, move the boom hoist into position to attach the
shackle to the adapter on the top position on the sling [43].
2) If using boom hoist, SPL-2430, move the boom hoist so that the holes in the
adapter assembly align with the holes in the lower attach bracket on the sling (View
D).
a) Install the two lockpins.
b) Install a retention pin in the end of each of the lockpins.
(d) Make sure that the full weight of the sleeve [21] is held by the boom hoist.
(e) Manually push the sleeve [21] aft and off the tracks.
(f) Put the sleeve [21] on a suitable pallet.

(b) For the outboard sleeve, make sure that the plugs are installed in the mounting holes.

blocker door is not taped and that the remaining blocker doors are taped against the wall
of the sleeve.

lower blocker door.

E. Translating Sleeve Outer-Skin-Panel Inspection
SUBTASK 78-31-02-210-004-F00
(1) Examine the outer-skin-panel on the translating sleeve for the damage that follows:
(a) Holes, cracks, nicks, gouges, delamination, dents and edge corrosion.
1) Cracks in the paint layer that do not affect the sealant or the structure of the panel
are acceptable.
2) If you find damage, refer to the SRM 54-30-01 for the permitted limits and repair
procedures.
F . Translating Sleeve Inner-Acoustic-Panel Inspection
SUBTASK 78-31-02-210-005-F00
(1) Look through the aft end of the fan duct to examine the aft end of the inner-acoustic-panel on
the translating sleeve for the damage that follows:
(a) Holes, cracks, nicks, gouges, delamination, dents and edge corrosion.
1) Cracks in the paint layer that do not affect the sealant or the structure of the panel
are acceptable.
2) If you find damage, refer to the SRM 54-30-01 for the permitted limits and repair
procedures.
(b) Pitting in the surface layer (small areas where the surface appears chipped away around
the perforation of the acoustic panel) (Figure 602).
NOTE: This pitting can occur during the usual manufacturing process of the acoustic
panel. This condition has been inspected and approved for in-service use at the
time of manufacture.
1) No action is necessary with the following conditions:
a) The surface area adjacent to each pitting location has the original silver finish
and does not show the black panel material.
b) There are no signs of edge erosion.
(c) Missing or damaged silver finish
1) Missing or damaged silver finish is acceptable if there is no damage to the resin
and/or fibers of the underlying panel.
2) Restore missing finish at the next available maintenance opportunity. Refer to CMM
78-31-24 Repair 1-1 to restore missing or damaged finish.
78-31-02

are acceptable.

(b) Pitting in the surface layer (small areas where the surface appears chipped away around

NOTE: This pitting can occur during the usual manufacturing process of the acoustic

1) No action is necessary with the following conditions:

4. Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task is for the removal of the upper locking hydraulic actuator.
(2) There are three hydraulic actuators on each torque box of the left and right thrust reversers on
an engine.
78-31-03
(3) The upper hydraulic actuator is a locking actuator, the middle and lower hydraulic actuators are
non-locking actuators.
(4) The upper locking hydraulic actuator will be referred to as the upper locking actuator for this
task.

(1) Disconnect the electrical connectors from the Linear Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT)

(a) For the left thrust reverser, disconnect the electrical connectors, D30072 and D30076.

H. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-001-F00
(1) Install the fire seal [30] and fire shield [29] on the upper locking actuator [1] (View H,
Figure 401).
(a) Put the fire seal [30] in the fire shield [29].
(b) Put the fire seal [30] and fire shield [29] over the rod end of the upper locking actuator [1].
1) Make sure that the fire seal [30] will contact the forward side of the torque box.
78-31-03
I. Install the Upper Locking Actuator
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-002-F00
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL THE UPPER-LOCKING ACTUATOR. THE
PUSH ROD WILL MOVE THOUGH AN OPENING IN THE TORQUE BOX AND
THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING. DO NOT LET THE PUSH ROD HIT THE
TORQUE BOX OR THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY , DAMAGE TO THE PUSH ROD CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE ROD END OF THE UPPER LOCKING ACTUATOR TURN
AFTER YOU RELEASE THE ACTUATOR LOCK. IF THE ROD END TURNS, IT
CAN CHANGE THE RIGGING OF THE HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR.
(1) Install the upper locking actuator [1] (View B, Figure 401).
(a) Unlock the upper locking actuator [1].
1) Remove the rig shipping pin from the rig pin hole in the proximity sensor bracket
and feedback rod end (if applicable).
2) Move the manual unlock lever [5] forward.
3) Hold the manual unlock lever in the forward position as you push the detent pin in.
4) Release the manual unlock lever.
(b) To extend the rod end, pull the rod end out by hand.
NOTE: Do not let the rod end turn when you extend it manually. Make sure that you hold
the rod end when you extend the actuator manually. Do not use hydraulic power
to extend the rod end.
NOTE: If necessary, thread a rag through the rod end bushing to provide grip as an aid
during extension. Make sure you do not let the rod end turn.
1) For the inboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 10 in. (254 mm).
2) For the outboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 21 in. (533 mm).
(c) Carefully insert the rod end through the opening in the torque box and aft cascade
support ring.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-410-010-F00
WARNING
OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE PROCEDURE TO CLOSE THE THRUST
REVERSERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do this task: Close the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-804-F00.
NOTE: If you close the thrust reverser, it will make the attachment of the rod end of the upper
locking actuator and the installation of the access door easier.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-026-F00
(3) Manually extend the applicable thrust reverser sleeve. Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation
- Extend (Manual Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-003-F00
(4) Install the two gimbal pins [19] that attach the upper locking actuator [1] to the gimbal ring on
the aft side of the torque box (View F , Figure 401).
(a) Apply grease, D00633, on the shanks of the two gimbal pins [19].
78-31-03
(b) Align the attachment holes in the upper locking actuator [1] and the gimbal ring.
(c) If you use the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42], to compress the fire seal [30]
against the torque box, do these steps (View I, Figure 401):
NOTE: Use a 3/16-inch allen wrench to turn the clamp block screws and use a 1/4-inch
allen wrench to turn the adjustment screw.
1) If not already done, loosen the clamp block screws [40] sufficiently so that the clamp
block will fit over the upper locking actuator [1].
2) Make sure that the adjustment screw [41] is retracted.
NOTE: The adjustment screw is on the forward end of the tool.
3) Tilt the aft end of the clamp assembly tool down and over the aft cascade support
ring.
4) Lower the forward end of the clamp assembly tool until the clamp block engages the
upper locking actuator [1].
5) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to move the clamp block aft.
a) Move the clamp block until the aft edge touches where the diameter of the
upper locking actuator [1] increases.
6) Tighten the clamp block screws [40].
7) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to compress the fire seal [30] against the torque
box.
8) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes.
(d) To manually compress the fire seal [30] against the torque box, do these steps:
1) Push aft on the forward end of the upper locking actuator [1] to compress the fire
seal against the torque box.
2) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes.
(e) Install the two gimbal pins [19].
1) Install a washer [21] and bolt [20] in each of the gimbal pins [19].
a) Tighten the bolts to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
(f) If the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42], was used, loosen the adjustment
screw [41] and clamp block screws [40] to remove the tool.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-016-F00
(5) Align the rod end of the upper locking actuator [1] with the clevis on the attach fitting (View E,
Figure 401).

(8) Do these steps to manually retract the applicable thrust reverser:
(a) T emporarily install the sync shaft and tubing. Do these steps:
NOTE: To manually retract the thrust reverser, the sync shafts must be temporarily
installed.
1) Do this task: Sync Shaft - Inspection/Check, TASK 78-31-04-200-801-F00.
2) If there is contamination, remove the contamination from the sync shaft with a
cotton wiper, G00034.
3) Move the coupling nut and tube adaptor along the tubing.
4) Insert the sync shaft into the tubing.
a) Make sure that the sync shaft engages the internal spline in the middle
actuator port.
5) Flex the sync shaft and insert the opposite end into the internal spline in the upper
locking actuator port.
78-31-03
6) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) - 945 in-lb (107 N·m).
NOTE: This is a temporary installation and it is not necessary to double-torque the
coupling nuts.
(b) Connect the retract line flexhose [6] to the union [9].
1) Tighten the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32 N·m).
2) Loosen the coupling nut.
3) Tighten the coupling nut again to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32 N·m).
(c) Connect the extend line flexhose [7] to the upper extend port.
1) Tighten the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) - 945 in-lb (107 N·m).
2) Loosen the coupling nut.
3) Tighten the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) - 945 in-lb (107 N·m).
(d) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-804-F00.

(10) Connect the hydraulic lines to the upper locking actuator [1] (View B and View C, Figure 401).
(a) Remove the protective covers from the hydraulic lines and the actuator ports.
(b) Connect the upper retract hydraulic line [2] to the union [3].
1) Hand tighten the coupling nut at this time.
2) Tighten the two bolts on the clamp block that hold the upper retract hydraulic
line [2].
a) Tighten the bolts to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
3) Tighten the coupling nut on the upper retract hydraulic line [2].
a) Tighten the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32 N·m).
b) Loosen the coupling nut.
c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) - 283 in-lb (32 N·m).

6. Middle Hydraulic Actuator Removal
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This task is for the removal of the middle hydraulic actuator.
(2) There are three hydraulic actuators on each torque box of the left and right thrust reversers on
an engine.
(3) The upper hydraulic actuator is a locking actuator, the middle and lower hydraulic actuators are
non-locking actuators.

and if the sleeve is fully extended, the tool will be easier to use.

(11) Do these steps to drain the hydraulic fluid from the hydraulic lines (View F):
NOTE: To decrease hydraulic fluid spray when the coupling nuts are loosened, wrap cotton
wiper, G00034, around the wrench, nut and hydraulic line.
(a) Wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the electrical connector on the sync lock receptacle
on the lower actuator.
NOTE: The cloth will catch the hydraulic fluid and prevent damage to the electrical
connector.
(b) Loosen the two bolts on each of the two clampblocks that hold the lower hydraulic retract
line.
NOTE: To remove the sleeve fitting on the hydraulic retract line from the actuator port,
the hydraulic retract line must be carefully flexed. If the clampblocks are loose,
the hydraulic retract line can be flexed easier.
(c) Disconnect the hydraulic retract line at the lower actuator.
1) Carefully remove the sleeve fitting on the hydraulic retract line from the actuator
port.
2) Let the hydraulic fluid drain into the 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant
container, STD-1110.
(d) Disconnect the coupling nut on the sync shaft tubing at the lower actuator.
1) Let the hydraulic fluid drain in a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container,
STD-1110.
(e) Re-connect the coupling nut for the lower sync shaft to the lower actuator.
1) Torque the coupling nut to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) to 945 in-lb (107 N·m).
2) Loosen the coupling nut.
3) Torque the coupling nut again to 855 in-lb (97 N·m) to 945 in-lb (107 N·m).
(f) Re-connect the coupling nut for the lower retract line to the lower actuator.
1) Torque the coupling nut to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m).
2) Loosen the coupling nut.
3) Torque the coupling nut again to 256 in-lb (29 N·m) to 283 in-lb (32 N·m).

CAUTION

(1) Do these steps to install the middle actuator [51]:
NOTE: Recommended to not turn the actuator rod end. For actuators without an Linear
Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT), accidental rotation of the rod end will not
cause detrimental effects.
(a) To extend the rod end of the middle actuator [51], pull the rod end out by hand:
NOTE: Do not let the rod end turn when you extend it manually. Make sure that you hold
the rod end when you extend the actuator manually. Do not use hydraulic power
to extend the rod end.
NOTE: If necessary, thread a rag through the rod end bushing to provide grip as an aid
during extension. Make sure you do not let the rod end turn.
1) For the inboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 10 in. (254 mm).
2) For the outboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 21 in. (533 mm).
(b) Carefully insert the rod end through the opening in the torque box and aft cascade
support ring.

8. Lower Hydraulic Actuator Removal
(Figure 403)
A. General
(1) This task is for the removal of the lower hydraulic actuator.
(2) There are three hydraulic actuators on each torque box of the left and right thrust reversers on
an engine.
(3) The upper hydraulic actuator is a locking actuator, the middle and lower hydraulic actuators are
non-locking actuators.

(10) Do these steps to expose the gimbal pins and to prepare for the use of the actuator removal
and installation tool:
NOTE: The thrust reverser sleeve must be extended to remove the gimbal pins from the aft

78-31-03
(a) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps to manually extend the thrust
reverser sleeve:
1) Manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve no more than 10 in. (254 mm) from the
forward edge of the torque box.
a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
(b) For the outboard thrust reverser sleeve, manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve to the
fully extended position.
NOTE: The outboard thrust reverser sleeve will not touch the leading edge of the wing
and if the sleeve is fully extended, the tool will be easier to use.
1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-019-F00
WARNING
DO NOT INSTALL PRESSURE CAPS TO THE HYDRAULIC LINES THAT
CONNECT TO CONTROL VALVE MODULE PORTS TO DEACTIVATE THE
THRUST REVERSER. THE THRUST REVERSER CAN OPERATE WHEN
PRESSURIZED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHES AND GLOVES
WHEN YOU DO WORK ON THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. HYDRAULIC FLUID
CAN CAUSE A LEAK FROM THE OPEN PORTS OF THE COMPONENT OR
FROM THE HYDRAULIC LINES. INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON THE THRUST REVERSER OR
ENGINE COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN A COMPONENT IF
HYDRAULIC FLUID GETS ON IT . HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE
TO THE EQUIPMENT .
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO LOOSEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUT . USE ONE
TO HOLD THE FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO LOOSEN THE COUPLING NUT .
IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(11) Do these steps to drain the hydraulic fluid from the hydraulic lines (View B):
NOTE: To decrease hydraulic fluid spray when the coupling nuts are loosened, wrap cotton
wiper, G00034, around the wrench, nut and hydraulic line.
(a) Wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the electrical connector on the sync lock receptacle
on the lower actuator.
NOTE: The cloth will catch the hydraulic fluid and prevent damage to the electrical
connector.
(b) Loosen the two bolts on each of the two clampblocks that hold the lower hydraulic retract
line [132].
NOTE: To remove the sleeve fitting on the hydraulic retract line from the actuator port,
the hydraulic retract line must be carefully flexed. If the clampblocks are loose,
the hydraulic retract line can be flexed easier.
78-31-03
(c) Disconnect the lower hydraulic retract line [132] at the lower actuator [103].
1) Carefully remove the sleeve fitting on the lower hydraulic retract line [132] from the
actuator port.
2) Let the hydraulic fluid drain in a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container,
STD-1110.
(d) Disconnect the coupling nut on the sync shaft tubing at the lower actuator [103].
1) Let the hydraulic fluid drain into the 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant
container, STD-1110.
2) Move the coupling nut and tube adapter back along the tubing to get access to the
sync shaft end.
3) Flex the sync shaft to remove it from the internal splined port in the lower
actuator [103].
CAUTION
DO NOT LET DIRT OR OTHER CONTAMINATION GET ON THE
SYNC SHAFT . DAMAGE TO THE SYNC SHAFT CAN OCCUR.
4) Remove the sync shaft.
a) Make sure that dirt or contamination does not get on the sync shaft.
(e) Remove the union [110] and packing [111] from the upper retract port of the lower
actuator (View B).
1) Keep the union [110] for the subsequent installation and discard the packing [111].
CAUTION
USE ONLY HOLLOW CORE CAPS TO COVER THE ACTUATOR PORTS.
IF YOU DO NOT , INTERNAL DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(f) Install protective covers on the hydraulic lines and actuator ports.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-039-F00
(12) Do these steps to remove the sync lock [105]:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the sync lock receptacle (View B):
1) For the left thrust reverser, disconnect the electrical connector D1008.
2) For the right thrust reverser, disconnect the electrical connector D1016.
(b) Remove the nut [106] and washer [107] from the adapter plug [108].
NOTE: You do not have to remove the two bolts that hold the bracket to the sync lock.
After the coupling nut is loose, the bracket will move off the stud.
(c) Loosen the coupling nut on the sync lock [105].
(d) Remove the sync lock [105] and bracket.
(e) Remove the adapter plug [108] and packing [109].
1) Discard the packing [109].
(f) Install protective covers on the sync lock [105] and lower actuator [103].

H. Lower Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-040-F00
(1) Do these steps to remove the two gimbal pins [120] that attach the lower actuator [103] to the
gimbal ring on the aft side of the torque box (View E):
(a) If you use the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] to remove the gimbal
pins [120], do these steps (View I):
NOTE: Use a allen wrench, STD-7895 to turn the clamp block screws [40] and use a 1/4
inch allen wrench, STD-14286 to turn the adjustment screw [41].
1) If not already done, loosen the clamp block screws [40] sufficiently so that the clamp
block will fit over the lower actuator [103].
2) Make sure that the adjustment screw [41] is retracted.
NOTE: The adjustment screw is on the forward end of the tool.
3) Tilt the aft end of the clamp assembly tool down and over the aft cascade support
ring.
4) Lower the forward end of the clamp assembly tool until the clamp block engages the
lower actuator [103].
5) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to move the clamp block aft.
a) Move the clamp block until the aft edge touches where the diameter of the
lower actuator [103] increases.
6) Tighten the clamp block screws [40].
7) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque
box.
(b) Remove a bolt [121] and washer [122] from each of the two gimbal pins [120].
1) Remove the two gimbal pins [120].
(c) If the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] was used, loosen the adjustment
screw [41] and clamp block screws [40] to remove the tool.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-011-F00
(2) Do these steps to remove the access door [116] and disconnect the rod end of the lower
actuator [103] (View D):
(a) To remove the applicable access doors [116], remove the nine bolts [115].

(3) Do these steps to get the necessary clearance to remove the lower actuator [103]:
(a) For the inboard thrust reverser, do these steps to open the thrust reverser:
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are completely retracted.
NOTE: Without hydraulics to hold the flaps in the retract position, the weight of the
flaps can cause them to extend a small amount.
2) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser as it is opened to make sure that it does
not touch the leading edge of the wing.
3) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
(b) For the outboard thrust reverser, open the thrust reverser, do this task: Open the Thrust
Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
NOTE: The outboard thrust reverser will not touch the leading edge of the wing.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-010-012-F00
CAUTION
WHEN YOU INSTALL THE LOWER ACTUATOR, YOU WILL MOVE THE PUSH
ROD THOUGH AN OPENING IN THE TORQUE BOX AND THE AFT CASCADE
SUPPORT RING. DO NOT LET THE PUSH ROD HIT THE TORQUE BOX OR
THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING, DAMAGE TO THE PUSH ROD CAN
OCCUR.
(4) Carefully remove the lower actuator [103].
SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-022-F00
(5) After you remove the lower actuator [103], do these steps:
(a) Remove the fire shield [124] and the fire seal [123] from the lower actuator (View F).
1) Examine the fire seal [123] for damage.
2) If you find no damage, keep the fire seal for the subsequent installation.
3) If you find damage, replace the fire seal [123].

SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-011-F00
(1) Do these steps to install the fire seal [123] and fire shield [124] on the lower actuator [103]
(View F):
(a) Put the fire seal [123] in the fire shield [124].
(b) Put the fire seal [123] and fire shield [124] over the rod end of the lower actuator [103].
1) Make sure that the fire seal [123] will contact the forward side of the torque box.
I. Install the Lower Hydraulic Actuator
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-012-F00
CAUTION
WHEN YOU INSTALL THE LOWER ACTUATOR, YOU WILL MOVE THE PUSH
ROD THOUGH AN OPENING IN THE TORQUE BOX AND THE AFT CASCADE
SUPPORT RING. DO NOT LET THE PUSH ROD HIT THE TORQUE BOX OR
THE AFT CASCADE SUPPORT RING, DAMAGE TO THE PUSH ROD CAN
OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to install the lower actuator [103]:
NOTE: Recommended to not turn the actuator rod end. For actuators without an Linear
Variable Differential Transformer (LVDT), accidental rotation of the rod end will not
cause detrimental effects.
(a) To extend the rod end of the lower actuator [103], pull the rod end out by hand:
NOTE: Do not let the rod end turn when you extend it manually. Make sure that you hold
the rod end when you extend the actuator manually. Do not use hydraulic power
to extend the rod end.
NOTE: If necessary, thread a rag through the rod end bushing to provide grip as an aid
during extension. Make sure you do not let the rod end turn.
1) For the inboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 10 in. (254 mm).
2) For the outboard thrust reverser, extend the rod end approximately 21 in. (533 mm).
(b) Carefully insert the rod end through the opening in the torque box and aft cascade
support ring.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-860-005-F00
WARNING
OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE PROCEDURE TO CLOSE THE THRUST
REVERSERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do this task: Close the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-804-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-013-F00
(3) Do these steps to install the two gimbal pins [120] that attach the lower actuator [103] to the
gimbal ring on the aft side of the torque box (View E):
(a) Apply grease, D00633 on the shanks of the two gimbal pins [120].
(b) Align the attachment holes in the lower actuator [103] and the gimbal ring.
78-31-03
(c) If you use the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] to compress the fire
seal [123] against the torque box, do these steps (View I):
NOTE: Use a 1/4-inch allen wrench to turn the adjustment screw and use a 3/16-inch
allen wrench to turn the clamp block screws.
1) If not already done, loosen the clamp block screws [40] sufficiently, so that the
clamp block will fit over the lower actuator [103].
2) Make sure that the adjustment screw [41] is retracted.
NOTE: The adjustment screw is on the forward end of the tool.
3) Tilt the aft end of the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] down and over
the aft cascade support ring.
4) Lower the forward end of the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] until the
clamp block engages the lower actuator [103].
5) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to move the clamp block aft.
a) Move the clamp block until the aft edge touches where the diameter of the
lower actuator [103] increases.
6) Tighten the clamp block screws [40].
7) Tighten the adjustment screw [41] to compress the fire seal [123] against the torque
box.
8) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes.
(d) To manually compress the fire seal [123] against the torque box, do these steps:
1) Push aft on the forward end of the lower actuator [103] to compress the fire
seal [123] against the torque box.
2) Turn the housing one direction or the other to align the attachment holes.
(e) Install the two gimbal pins [120].
(f) Install a washer [122] and bolt [121] in each of the gimbal pins [120].
1) Tighten the bolts [121] to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) to 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
(g) If the clamp assembly actuator tool, SPL-2439 [42] was used, loosen the adjustment
screw [41] and clamp block screws [40] to remove the tool.

1. Thrust Reverser Upper Locking Actuator - Integrity Test
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task is used to make sure that the locking actuator is properly functioning.
(2) To engage the manual drive shaft in the sync lock [4], the lock release pin [3] in the 3/8 inch
square opening [2] at the end of the sync lock [4] must be pushed in.
(3) The sync lock [4] is connected to the lower hydraulic actuator, on the torque box.
(4) A training video is available in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) supplements to assist
with this task.

G. Thrust Reverser Upper Locking Actuator - Integrity Test
SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-013-F00
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
AREA AFT OF THE APPLICABLE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
STOP THE MANUAL EXTENSION IF THE THRUST REVERSER EXTENDS AT
AN ANGLE. THIS IS AN INDICATION THAT THERE ARE SYNC SHAFTS THAT
ARE BROKEN OR NOT INSTALLED. IF YOU CONTINUE, DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY MORE THAN 50 INCH-POUNDS OF TORQUE TO EXTEND
OR RETRACT THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO, DAMAGE TO THE
SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT ENGAGE THE MANUAL UNLOCK PIN ON
THE UPPER LOCKING HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR BY PREVIOUS
MAINTENANCE ACTIONS. THIS WILL PREVENT THE COMPLETION OF THE
INTEGRITY TEST . IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THIS CAUTION, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE THRUST REVERSER SLEEVE DOES NOT HIT THE
WING IF THE THRUST REVERSER IS IN THE 45-DEGREE OPEN POSITION.
DO NOT EXTEND THE INBOARD SLEEVE. DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
(1) Obey all of these WARNINGS and CAUTIONS when you do this procedure.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-016-F00
(2) Do these steps to release the lock for the upper actuator with the manual unlock handle
(Figure 501):
(a) Move the manual unlock lever forward.
(b) Hold the manual unlock lever in the forward position as you push the detent pin in.
(c) Release the manual unlock lever.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-014-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT HIT THE END OF THE SYNC LOCK OR THE 3/8 INCH DRIVE
WRENCH TO PUSH THE LOCK RELEASE PIN. DAMAGE TO THE SYNC
LOCK CAN OCCUR.
(3) Do these steps to unlock sync lock [4], engage manual drive, and to manually extend the thrust
reverser (Figure 502):
(a) For the standard hand tools:
1) Put a 3/8 inch square drive speed wrench, STD-997, or equivalent into the 3/8 inch
square opening [2].
NOTE: The 3/8 drive wrench will go into the opening approximately 0.30 in.
(7.62 mm).
78-31-03
2) Apply pressure until the lock release pin [3] goes in.
3) Use a standard wrench, STD-6760, or equivalent on the hex nut [1] at the end of the
sync lock [4] and slowly move a small amount, in one direction and then the other,
to help the lock release pin [3] go in.
NOTE: The open ended wrench is only needed to assist the 3/8 square-drive to go
in.
(b) For the fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641:
1) Put a 3/8 inch square drive speed wrench, STD-997, or equivalent into the 3/8-inch
square opening in the drive socket.
NOTE: The 3/8 drive wrench will go into the opening approximately 0.30 in.
(7.62 mm).
2) Mate the socket with the hex nut [1] on the end of the sync lock [4].
3) Apply pressure until the lock release pin [3] goes in.
4) Move the fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641, a small amount in one direction
and then the other, to help the lock release pin [3] go in.
CAUTION
WHILE YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS
PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE-DRIVE
WRENCH. THIS MAKES SURE THAT THE LOCK RELEASE PIN IS
PUSHED IN. THIS WILL KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF
YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER AND YOU DO NOT FULLY
ENGAGE THE MANUAL DRIVE, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN
OCCUR.
(c) From the fully stowed position of the thrust reverser sleeve, manually extend the thrust
reverser by gradually applying a continuous torque of up to 50 in-lb (6 N·m).
1) To extend the right reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise.
2) To extend the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counter clockwise.
(d) If the thrust reverser is in the 45-degree open position, do these steps:
1) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps:
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are fully retracted.
b) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser sleeve.
<1> Make sure that it does not touch the wing.
(e) Make sure that the thrust reverser sleeves operate smoothly.
NOTE: Thrust reverser needs to be extended at least 10 in. (254 mm) from the fully
stowed position.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-017-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT HIT THE END OF THE SYNC LOCK OR THE 3/8 INCH DRIVE
WRENCH TO PUSH THE LOCK RELEASE PIN. DAMAGE TO THE SYNC
LOCK CAN OCCUR.
(4) Do these steps to retract the thrust reverser (Figure 502):
78-31-03
CAUTION
AS YOU RETRACT THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS
PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE DRIVE
WRENCH TO KEEP THE LOCK RELEASE PIN PUSHED IN. THIS WILL
KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF YOU RETRACT THE
THRUST REVERSER WHEN THE MANUAL DRIVE IS NOT FULLY
ENGAGED, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN OCCUR.
(a) To retract the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise.
(b) To retract the right thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counterclockwise.
NOTE: The sleeve will be at the manual track limit when you hear the override clutch on
the manual drive make a "ratcheting" sound. If the locking actuator has not
locked at this time, hydraulic power will be necessary to completely retract and
lock the thrust reverser.
1) If it is necessary to use hydraulic power to completely retract and lock the thrust
reverser, then do these steps:
a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance,
TASK 78-31-00-440-803-F00.
b) Do the applicable steps in this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract
(Power Procedure), TASK 78-31-00-980-806-F00.
c) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance,
TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00.
(c) Make sure that the thrust reverser sleeves operate smoothly.
(d) Make sure that manual drive unit is turned until the thrust reverser sleeves are fully
retracted.
(e) Put the upper locking actuator to the locked position with the manual unlock handle.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-980-018-F00
(5) Do these steps to make sure that thrust reverser upper locking actuator operates correctly.
(a) Make sure that the upper actuator with the manual unlock is locked.
NOTE: To completely retract and lock the thrust reverser, it can be necessary to use
hydraulic power. You can use a wrench to partially retract the thrust reverser,
however if the locking actuator does not lock, hydraulic power will be necessary
to completely retract and lock the thrust reverser.
CAUTION
WHILE YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER, APPLY CONTINUOUS
PRESSURE ON THE LOCK RELEASE PIN WITH THE SQUARE-DRIVE
WRENCH. THIS MAKES SURE THAT THE LOCK RELEASE PIN IS
PUSHED IN. THIS WILL KEEP THE MANUAL DRIVE FULLY ENGAGED. IF
YOU EXTEND THE THRUST REVERSER AND YOU DO NOT FULLY
ENGAGE THE MANUAL DRIVE, DAMAGE TO THE SYNC LOCK CAN
OCCUR.
(b) From the fully stowed position of the thrust reverser sleeve, try to manually extend the
thrust reverser by gradually applying a continuous torque of up to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) or until
you hear the override clutch on the sync lock manual drive making the “ratcheting” sound.
1) To extend the right reverser sleeve, turn the wrench clockwise.
2) To extend the left thrust reverser sleeve, turn the wrench counter clockwise.
(c) If the thrust reverser is in the 45-degree open position, do these steps:
78-31-03
1) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps:
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are fully retracted.
b) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser sleeve.
<1> If it extends, make sure that it does not touch the wing.
(d) Make sure that the thrust reverser does not deploy.
NOTE: If the thrust reverser sleeve stays in the fully stowed position, the thrust reverser
upper locking actuator is serviceable.
NOTE: Some movement of the thrust reverser sleeve can occur near the lower hydraulic
actuator. This is because of the wind up in the flexible shafts between the sync
lock and the lock of the upper locking hydraulic actuator.
(e) Stop manual deployment, if the thrust reverser sleeve starts to deploy.
NOTE: If a thrust reverser sleeve can be manually translated, the upper locking hydraulic
actuator is not serviceable.
1) Replace the upper locking hydraulic actuator before the next flight, do these tasks:
a) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00,
b) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE TORQUE ON THE SYNC LOCK IS AT ZERO
BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE SQUARE-DRIVE WRENCH. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY , THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT THE THRUST REVERSER
CANNOT DEPLOY WHEN COMMANDED AND DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(f) Remove the square-drive wrench or fully depressed drive socket, SPL-18641, from the
sync lock [4].
(g) Make sure that the sync lock release pin [3] does not stay in the pushed in condition,
after the square-drive wrench is removed.

G. Manual Unlock Handle Assembly Rigging
SUBTASK 78-31-03-820-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to align the manual unlock handle assembly [1]:
(a) Install the torsion spring [8] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1].
1) Install one leg of the torsion spring [8] in the hole on the manual unlock handle
assembly [1].
(b) Install the unlock lever [7] in the locked position on the actuator housing [13] (Figure 602)
(Sheet 5 or 6).
(c) Align the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with the mark (locked position) and insert
the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through the bushing [21] until the splines just
engage.
1) Pull the free leg of the torsion spring [8] around to align it with the hole in the
actuator housing [13].
2) Push the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through until it bottoms on the
bushing [21].
a) Make sure that the torsion spring [8] is installed correctly.
(d) Install the shim [5] with the counterbore towards the actuator housing [13] (Figure 603).
1) Measure the gap G between the shim [5] and the bushing [20].
a) If gap G is more than 0.004 in. (0.102 mm), then make a new shim [5].
b) If there is no gap so that the shim [5] face is in contact with the bushing [20],
then trim the shim [5].
<1> Measure F , the distance from the shoulder end of the lockout handle
shaft, and subtract 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) from F to get the shim
thickness (S3).
<2> Trim the shim [5] face that makes contact with bushing [20] to obtain the
S3 thickness (the gap tolerance is 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) - 0.004 in.
(0.102 mm)).
NOTE: A new shim [5] will be oversized. The new shim [5] face will be
in contact with the bushing [20]. You will need to trim the new
shim [5] to obtain the 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) gap.
(e) Install and tighten nut [6] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m).
(f) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position and release the
manual unlock handle assembly [1] (Figure 605).
1) Make sure that the manual unlock handle assembly [1] moves back smoothly.
(g) Make sure that the unlock lever [7] and manual unlock handle assembly [1] operate
correctly with no binding.
(h) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back in the locked position.
(i) Make sure that the actuator is in the stowed and locked position.
1) Remove the nine bolts [14] from the access panel cover [15].
2) Remove access panel cover [15] from the TR sleeve [19] to get access to the
actuator rod end [18].
3) Make sure that the gland nut [17] is within 0.007 in. (0.18 mm) - 0.033 in. (0.84 mm)
of the rod stop [16].
78-31-03
(j) Do these steps to install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]

E. Freeplay Check
SUBTASK 78-31-03-220-002-F00
(1) Do one of these procedures to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit is
within limits:
(a) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit:
1) From the locked position, move the manual unlock handle assembly [1] aft until it
stops.
2) Use an angular measurement tool to measure the manual unlock handle
assembly [1] free-play (Figure 605).
3) If the free-play is less than or equal to 9.40 degrees, continue with the procedure to
replace the manual unlock handle assembly [1].
4) If the free-play is more than 9.40 degrees, replace the actuator. Do these tasks:
a) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00
b) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
(b) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit with the
free play gauge, SPL-18803 (C78042-23) (Figure 606 (Sheet 1)):
1) Install the gauge assembly on the upper locking hydraulic actuator.
2) Attach the gauge assembly to the actuator housing by inserting the index pin into
the applicable hole in the actuator housing.
a) Align the assembly to secure it to the actuator housing using captive screw.
78-31-03
3) Make sure that the slide cutout edge labeled "START" touches the unlock handle.
NOTE: The unlock handle of the manual unlock handle assembly [1] should be in
the forward stop position.
a) If it is necessary, push the unlock handle lightly in the forward direction until it
stops.
b) Do not move the manual unlock handle.
4) With the slide in the adjusted position, tighten knob to secure gauge assembly.
5) Push the manual unlock handle aft until it stops.
a) If the manual unlock handle touches the FAIL edge, replace the actuator.
b) If the actuator needs to be replaced, do these tasks:
<1> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal,
TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00
<2> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation,
TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
(c) Do these steps to verify the manual unlock handle assembly [1] free-play limit with the
free play gauge, SPL-18803 (C78042-17) (Figure 606 (Sheet 2)):
1) Make sure that the correct side of the Go/Fail slide is used for each upper locking
hydraulic actuator.
NOTE: Each side of the Go/Fail slide is marked with the actuator part number(s)
that it can be used with.
2) If an incorrect side of the tool faces the actuator, loosen the top knob to allow
rotation of the Go/Fail slide, then hand tighten the top knob.
3) Install free play gauge, SPL-18803, onto the manual unlock handle side of the
upper locking hydraulic actuator at the two threaded holes.
a) The un-threaded pin slides into the top threaded hole closest to the manual
unlock handle, the threaded knob screws into the bottom threaded hole.
4) Loosen the top knob and move the Go/Fail slide forward or aft until the GO edge
makes contact with the manual unlock handle flange.
a) When the Go/Fail slide is in position, tighten the top knob.
b) Do not move the manual unlock handle.
5) Push the manual unlock handle aft until it stops.
a) If the manual unlock handle makes contact with the FAIL edge, replace the
actuator.
b) If the actuator needs to be replaced, do these tasks:
<1> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal,
TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00
<2> Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation,
TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
(d) Do the steps that follow to measure the manual unlock handle assembly free-play:
1) Measure the radial height by locating a point on the manual unlock handle assembly
and measuring the distance from the handle axis to this point. A point from
Table 601 can be used.
78-31-03

F . Procedure
SUBTASK 78-31-03-860-014-F00
(1) For on-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1], do these steps:
WARNING
DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE TO PREVENT THE OPERATION
OF THE THRUST REVERSER. THE ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE
THRUST REVERSER CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance,
TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00.
(b) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
(c) Make sure the thrust reverser sleeve is in the stowed and locked position.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-200-001-F00
(2) Do these steps to verify the lock handle freeplay limit is within limits:
78-31-03
(a) Measure and mark the measurement point on the locking actuator unlock handle denoted
(X) in Figure 804. This point is 2.15 ±0.01 in. (54.61 ±0.25 mm) from the center of the
handle axis of rotation.
(b) Clamp or fix the dial indicator in a location that allows for lateral measurement of that
point.
NOTE: If the dial indicator is setup opposite to that in Figure 804, zero the dial indicator
when the handle is pushed in the forward direction, and measure the deflection
when the handle is pushed aft.
(c) Push the unlock handle aft until it stops (1
st point). Zero the dial indicator.
(d) Press lightly on the unlock handle towards the Forward direction until it stops (2 nd point).
Do not unlock the actuator.
(e) If the dial indicator reads less than or equal to 0.095 in. (2.413 mm), the Manual Unlock
Handle Assembly Replacement may continue.
(f) If this difference is greater than 0.095 in. (2.413 mm), replace the actuator. These are the
tasks:
1) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00.
2) Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator - Installation, TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-000-003-F00
(3) For off-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1]:
(a) Do this task: Upper Locking Hydraulic Actuator Removal, TASK 78-31-03-000-801-F00.
(b) Retract and lock the actuator.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-020-048-F00
(4) Do these steps to remove the defective manual unlock handle assembly [1]:
(a) Mark the position of the handle relative to the actuator housing so that the new handle
assembly is installed in the same position.
1) In the locked position, the handle lever is approximately vertical to the axis of the
actuator.
(b) Remove the two screws [9] that attach the detent housing [2] to the actuator housing [13].
(c) Remove the detent housing [2], manual unlock pin [10], spring [11], and spring guide [12].
(d) Remove the nut [6] from the manual unlock handle assembly [1].
(e) Remove the shim [5], unlock lever [7], torsion spring [8], and manual unlock handle
assembly [1].
(f) Do not remove the two bushings.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-420-038-F00
(5) Do these steps to install the new manual unlock handle assembly [1]:
(a) Install the torsion spring [8] on the new manual unlock handle assembly [1].
1) Locate one leg of the spring in the hole.
(b) Install the unlock lever [7] in the locked position in the actuator housing [13] (Figure 801)
(Sheet 3).
(c) Align the manual unlock handle assembly [1] with the mark (locked position) and insert
the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through the bushing until the splines just engage.
1) Pull the free leg of the torsion spring [8] around to align with the hole in the actuator
housing [13].
78-31-03
2) Push the manual unlock handle assembly [1] through until it bottoms on the
bushing [21].
3) Make sure the torsion spring [8] is installed correctly.
(d) Install the shim [5] with the counterbore towards the actuator housing [13] (Figure 802).
1) Measure the gap G between the shim [5] and the bushing [20].
a) If the gap G is more than 0.004 in. (0.102 mm), make a new shim [5].
b) If there is no gap and the shim face is in contact with the bushing [20], shim [5]
must be trimmed.
<1> Measure F (the distance from the shoulder end of the unlock handle
shaft) and subtract 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) to get S3 (the shim thickness).
<2> Trim the shim face that contacts the bushing [20] to obtain the S3
thickness (the gap tolerance is 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) - 0.004 in.
(0.102 mm).
NOTE: A new shim is oversized. The shim face will be in contact with
the bushing and requires trimming to obtain the 0.002 in.
(0.051 mm) inch gap.
(e) Install the nut [6] and tighten the nut to 20-30 inch-pounds (2.26-3.39 newton-meters):
(f) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position and make sure the
unlock lever [7] and manual unlock handle assembly [1] operate correctly with no binding.
(g) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position and make sure
the actuator is in the stowed and locked position.
1) Remove the nine bolts [14] from the access panel cover [15].
2) Remove the access panel cover [15] on the TR sleeve [19] to get access to the
actuator rod end [18].
3) Make sure that the gland nut [17] is within 0.007-0.033 inch (0.1778-0.8382 mm) of
the rod stop [16].
(h) Do these steps to install the detent housing [2]:
1) Install the spring guide [12], spring [11], manual unlock pin [10], and detent
housing [2] in the actuator housing [13].
2) Install the two screws [9] that attach the detent housing [2] to the actuator
housing [13].
3) Tighten the two screws [9] to 27-30 inch-pounds (3.05-3.39 newton-meters).
4) Install lockwire to the screws [9].
(i) Pull the manual unlock handle assembly [1] to the unlocked position, then push and
release the manual unlock pin [10].
1) Make sure there is no binding and the manual unlock pin [10] springs back
smoothly.
(j) Put the manual unlock handle assembly [1] back to the locked position and make sure
the actuator is in the stowed and locked position.
1) Look through the access area and see if the rod stop [16] is in contact with the
gland nut [17].
(k) Do these steps to install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1]
(Figure 803):
78-31-03
1) Use the proximity sensor locator, SPL-4156 or gap gauge, SPL-13657, to position
the target [3] on the handle.
2) Apply and keep a slight pressure to the handle in the unlock position (light pressure
against internal lock sleeve, but do not move sleeve).
3) The target [3] must be 0.33-0.37 inch (8.38-9.40 mm) from the center of the bracket
sensor hole.
NOTE: Do not exceed a distance greater than 0.37 inches (9.40 mm) between the
target [3] and bracket sensor hole. It could lead to a false locked actuator
indication.
4) Install the target [3] on the manual unlock handle assembly [1].
G. Put The Airplane Back To Its Usual Condition

TASK 78-31-03-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-03-710-009-F00
(3) For on-wing replacement of the manual unlock handle assembly [1], do these checks:
WARNING
OBEY ALL OF THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS IN THE REFERENCED
PROCEDURE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS,
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Normal Operation Test, TASK 78-31-00-700-801-F00.
1) Operate the thrust reverser through the deploy and stow cycles until the sleeves
move smoothly.
2) Examine the thrust reverser area for hydraulic fluid leaks.
(b) Do this task: EEC TEST , TASK 73-21-00-700-804-F00.
NOTE: This check will make sure that the electrical connections for the LVDT's are
correct.
1) Make sure that no LVDT maintenance messages show.
a) If a maintenance message shows, do the applicable fault isolation task in the
Fault Isolation Manual for that maintenance message.
b) If no maintenance messages show, the electrical connections for the LVDT are
correct.

(7) Do these steps to drain the hydraulic fluid from the hydraulic lines:
NOTE: To decrease hydraulic fluid spray when the coupling nuts are loosened, wrap cotton
wiper, G00034, around the wrench, coupling nut and hydraulic line.
(a) Wrap cotton wiper, G00034, around the electrical connector on the sync lock receptacle

STD-1110.

actuator.
NOTE: This will let air into the hydraulic lines to let the hydraulic fluid drain.

SUBTASK 78-31-04-020-002-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT LET DIRT OR OTHER CONTAMINATION GET ON THE SYNC SHAFT .
DAMAGE TO THE SYNC SHAFT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to remove the upper or lower sync shaft [4]:
(a) Disconnect the coupling nuts at the two ends of the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3].
(b) Move the coupling nuts and tube adapters back along the tube to get access to the sync
shaft ends.
(c) Flex the sync shaft [4] to remove it from the internal splined port in the actuator port [1].
(d) Remove the sync shaft [4] and tube [2] or tube [3] together.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-004-F00
WARNING
INSTALL THE TUBING TEMPORARILY WITHOUT THE SYNC SHAFT . IF YOU
APPLY PRESSURE, THE TUBING WILL COLLECT THE HYDRAULIC FLUID. IF
YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do these steps to temporarily install the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3]:
(a) Put the upper tube [2] or lower tube [3], without the sync shaft [4], in its position between
the actuators.
(b) Tighten the coupling nuts to 855 in-lb (96.6 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.8 N·m).
NOTE: This is a temporary installation and it is not necessary to tighten, loosen, then
tighten again (double-torque) the coupling nuts.

3. Sync Shaft Installation
(Figure 401, Figure 402)
A. General
(1) After you install the sync shaft and tubing, you must do the thrust reverser normal operational
test.
(2) To correctly rig the sync shaft, hydraulic pressure must be applied to the retract side of the
thrust reverser actuators when the sync shaft is installed.
(3) The upper and lower sync shafts are interchangeable and can be reversed end for end.

SUBTASK 78-31-04-480-001-F00
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DEACTIVATE THE DEPLOY CONTROL CIRCUIT .
THIS WILL MAKE SURE THAT THE HYDRAULIC PRESSURE IS ON THE
RETRACT LINE ONLY . IF YOU DO NOT , THE TR SLEEVES CAN DEPLOY .
INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) To prevent the actuation of the deploy circuit, do these steps to connect the B78009-5 cable
assembly from the thrust reverser maintenance lock equipment, SPL-9002, to the control valve
module:
NOTE: The B78009-5 cable assembly is part of the thrust reverser maintenance lock
equipment. There are two -5 wire bundle cable assemblies in the B78009 tool.
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the applicable control valve module receptacle.
1) For Engine 1, disconnect the electrical connector, D03052.
2) For Engine 2, disconnect the electrical connector, D03056.
(b) Connect the P1 connector of the -5 cable assembly to the control valve module
receptacle.
(c) Connect the electrical connector to the J1 receptacle of the -5 cable assembly.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-860-005-F00
(2) Do these steps to supply hydraulic power to the retract side of the actuators:
(a) Make sure that the tube [2] and tube [3] are temporarily installed.
(b) Move the applicable reverse thrust lever up and aft to the extend (deploy) position.
NOTE: This will unlock the sync lock.
1) Install a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858.

CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
B 5 C00276 ENGINE 1 THRUST REVERSER CONT

WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY

D. Inspection the Sync Shaft
SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-005-F00
(1) Examine the sync shaft tubes for evidence of hydraulic fluid leaks.
(a) Tighten or replace sync shafts as necessary to stop any leaks that are found.
NOTE: If a leak is found in the lower sync shaft P/N 315A1825–25, replace the tube with
P/N 315A1805–29 or refer to Service Letter 737–SL-78–057–A.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-020-003-F00
(2) For the applicable sync shaft, do this task: Sync Shaft Removal, TASK 78-31-04-000-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-001-F00
(3) Use a hand held 5x magnifying lens, STD-3912 to do a visual inspection of the sync shaft
wires:
(a) Look for a broken wire.
1) If you find a broken wire, then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft
Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
(b) Look for wire strand separations.
1) If the width of the strand separation is equal to or less than the diameter of the wire
strand, then the sync shaft is acceptable.
2) If the width of the strand separation is greater than the diameter of the wire strand,
then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft Installation,
TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-002-F00
(4) Look for twists in the square ends of the sync shaft.
78-31-04
(a) If you find a twist in the square end, then replace the sync shaft; do this task: Sync Shaft
Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-003-F00
(5) Look for kinks in the sync shaft.
(a) If you find a kink that is less than or equal to 0.020 inch (0.508 mm), then the sync shaft
is acceptable.
(b) If you find a kink that is greater than 0.020 inch (0.508 mm), then replace the sync shaft;
do this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-210-004-F00
(6) Look for abraded or worn areas on the surface of the sync shaft.
(a) If you find abraded or worn areas, then calculate the amount of face wear W:
1) Measure the diameter D2 of the sync shaft at the maximum depth of the worn area.
2) Measure the diameter D1 of the sync shaft in an adjacent area that is not damaged.
3) Subtract diameter D2 from diameter D1 and then divide by 2.
NOTE: (D1 - D2) /2 = W.
(b) If the face wear W is less than or equal to 0.013 inch (0.330 mm), then the sync shaft is
acceptable.
(c) If the face wear W is greater than 0.013 inch (0.330 mm), then replace the sync shaft; do
this task: Sync Shaft Installation, TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-04-420-007-F00
(7) If the sync shaft is serviceable, do this task: Sync Shaft Installation,
TASK 78-31-04-400-801-F00.

(2) Do these steps to install the cascade that was identified in the table:
(a) Apply primer, C00259, to the fastener holes in the cascade, aft cascade support ring and
forward cascade support ring.
1) Let the primer dry for 30 minutes.
(b) Lubricate the bolts [2] with grease, D00633.
(c) Install in its position cascade [21], cascade [22], cascade [23], cascade [24],
cascade [25], cascade [26], cascade [27], cascade [28], cascade [29], cascade [30],
cascade [31], cascade [32], cascade [33], cascade [34], cascade [35], cascade [36],
cascade [37], cascade [38], cascade [39], cascade [40], cascade [41], cascade [42],
cascade [43], or cascade [44].
78-31-05
(d) Align the bolt holes in the cascade with the fastener holes in the aft cascade support ring
and the forward cascade support ring.
(e) Loosely install the bolts [2] with a washer [3] under the head of the bolt in each fastener
location (forward and aft) to temporarily hold the cascade in its position.
NOTE: Engage only one or two threads at this time.
(f) Hand tighten only the bolts [2] at the aft cascade support ring at this time.
(g) Do a check of the clearance between the cascade and the forward cascade support ring
on the torque box.
1) If the clearance is less than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm), continue at the steps below to
tighten the bolts.
2) If the clearance is more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm), do these steps to decrease the
clearance between the cascade and the forward cascade support ring.
NOTE: The shim thickness can not be more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm).
a) Remove the bolts [2].
b) Install the shims [1].
c) Make sure that the shim [1] thickness is not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm).
d) Install the bolts [2].
(h) Do a check of the clearance between the cascade and the aft cascade support ring.
1) If the clearance is less than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm), continue at the steps below to
tighten the bolts.
2) If the clearance is more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm), do these steps to decrease the
clearance between the cascade and the aft cascade support ring.
NOTE: The shim thickness can not be more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm).
a) Remove the bolts [2].
b) Install the shims [1].
c) Make sure that the shim [1] thickness is not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm).
d) Install the bolts [2].
(i) Tighten the bolts [2] at the forward and aft cascade support rings to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) -
75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).
(j) Loosen all of the bolts (forward and aft) one-half turn.
(k) Tighten the bolts [2] again to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).

78-31-05-200-801-F01Thrust Reverser Cascade Segments - ExaminationPDF p. 499

2. Thrust Reverser Cascade Segments - Examination
A. General
(1) The cascade segments are made of a graphite/epoxy material. The cascade segments are
mounted between the forward torque box and the aft mounting ring. When the thrust reverser
is stowed, the cascade segments are located between the outer and inner skin of the thrust
reverser sleeve.
(2) During reverse thrust, the strongbacks transfer the thrust load from the cascade vanes to the
forward torque box through the attachment flanges.

E. Thrust Reverser Cascade Segments Examination
SUBTASK 78-31-05-210-001-F00
(1) Examine the cascade segments for damage, tears, cracks or delaminated areas in the
cascade vanes, strongbacks and attachment flanges.
(a) If damage, tears, cracks or delaminated areas in the cascade vanes, strongbacks or
attachment flanges is found, replace the cascade segment. These are the tasks:
Cascade - Removal, TASK 78-31-05-000-801-F00, Cascade - Installation,
TASK 78-31-05-400-801-F00.
78-31-05
(b) Contact Boeing to report the kind of damage and delamination found for repair
disposition.
NOTE: If possible, document the damage with digital photographs that can be sent by
e-mail, or provide a sketch of the damage that can be faxed.

F . Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 78-31-06-010-004-F00
WARNING
DO THESE SPECIFIED TASKS IN THE CORRECT SEQUENCE BEFORE YOU
OPEN THE THRUST REVERSERS: RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE, DO THE
DEACTIVATION PROCEDURES FOR THE LEADING EDGE AND THE THRUST
REVERSER (FOR GROUND MAINTENANCE), AND OPEN THE FAN COWL
PANELS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE ABOVE SEQUENCE, INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
(a) Install the short thrust reverser lock, SPL-23566, on the extended piston rod.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-980-003-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT MANUALLY EXTEND THE INBOARD THRUST REVERSER SLEEVE
MORE THAN 10 INCHES. MAKE SURE THAT THE SLEEVE DOES NOT
TOUCH THE WING LEADING EDGE WHEN YOU EXTEND THE THRUST
REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do these steps to expose the hardware that attaches the drag link to the blocker door:
NOTE: The sleeve must be partially extended to release the load on the drag link and expose
the hardware that attaches the drag link to the blocker door.
(a) For the inboard thrust reverser sleeve, do these steps to manually extend the thrust
reverser sleeve:
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps are completely retracted.
NOTE: Without hydraulics to hold the flaps in the retract position, the weight of the
flaps can cause them to extend a small amount.
2) Monitor the position of the thrust reverser sleeve as it is extended to make sure that
it does not touch the leading edge of the wing.
3) Manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve no more than 10 in. (25.4 cm) from the
forward edge of the torque box.
4) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
(b) For the outboard thrust reverser sleeve, manually extend the thrust reverser sleeve
approximately to 10 in. (25.4 cm).
NOTE: The outboard thrust reverser sleeve will not touch the leading edge of the wing.
1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
G. Blocker Door Removal
SUBTASK 78-31-06-010-005-F00
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU PUT PROTECTION ON THE FAN DUCT WALLS AND
BLOCKER DOORS. DAMAGE CAN OCCUR IF A TOOL OR DRAG LINK HITS
THE WALL OR DOORS.
(1) Do these steps to disconnect the drag link [4] from the blocker door [1] (door 1 and 6), blocker
door [2] (door 2-4 and 7-9), or blocker door [3] (door 5 and 10):
(a) Put a protective mat, STD-585, in the fan duct.
78-31-06
(b) Put cotton wiper, G00034, around the anchor fitting and drag link [4] at the inner wall.
NOTE: When the drag link is disconnected from the blocker door, it can move forward or
aft and fall against the inner wall. This can cause damage to the inner wall
composite panel.
(c) Remove the nut [5], washer [6], washer [7], bushing [16], and bolt [8] from the control link.
(d) Put a tie strap through the spherical bearing to hold the ball in its position.
(e) Make sure that there is protection between the drag link and the inner wall.
(f) Use Vibration Damping T ape 434 tape, G02329, to hold the drag link against the inner
wall of the fan duct.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-020-001-F00
(2) Do these steps to remove the blocker door [1] (door 1 and 6), blocker door [2] (door 2-4 and
7-9), or blocker door [3] (door 5 and 10):
(a) Get access to the blocker door hinges from the front of the fan duct.
(b) Make sure that there is a protective mat, STD-585, in the fan duct.
(c) At the floating hinge, remove the bolt [11], two bushings [12], washer [13], anti-rotation
bracket [10], and nut [14].
(d) At the clamped hinge, remove the bolt [11], washer [13], washer [15], bushing [12], and
nut [14].
NOTE: The clamped hinge at blocker door [3] has the bushing [12] installed at the
threaded end of the bolt. The clamped hinge at blocker door [1] and blocker
door [2] has the bushing installed at the bolt head.
1) Remove the blocker door.

G. Blocker Door Installation
SUBTASK 78-31-06-420-001-F00
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU PUT PROTECTION ON THE FAN DUCT WALLS AND
BLOCKER DOORS. DAMAGE CAN OCCUR IF A TOOL OR DRAG LINK HITS
THE WALL OR DOORS.
(1) Do these steps to install the blocker door [1] (door 1 and 6), blocker door [2] (door 2-4 and
7-9), or blocker door [3] (door 5 and 10):
(a) To install the blocker door [1], blocker door [2], or blocker door [3], align the fastener
holes in the blocker door hinge and sleeve hinge fitting.
78-31-06
(b) At the floating hinge for the blocker door [1], blocker door [2], or blocker door [3], do these
steps (View F , Figure 401):
1) Install the bolt [11], anti-rotation bracket [10], two bushings [12], washer [13], and
nut [14].
a) Make sure that no more than three threads show at the end of the bolt.
b) Tighten the nut [14] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m).
(c) At the clamped hinge for the blocker door [1] and blocker door [2], do these steps (View
G, Figure 401):
1) Install the bolt [11], washer [13], washer [15], bushing [12], and nut [14].
a) Make sure that you install the bushing [12] and one washer [15] at the bolt
head, and three washers [13] at the nut [14].
b) Make sure that no more than three bolt threads show.
c) Tighten the nut [14] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m).
(d) At the clamped hinge for blocker door [3], do these steps (View H, Figure 401):
1) Install the bolt [11], washer [13], washer [15], bushing [12], and nut [14].
a) Make sure that you install one washer [15] at the bolt head, and bushing [12]
and three washers [13] at the nut [14].
b) Make sure that no more than three bolt threads show.
c) Tighten the nut [14] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 78-31-06-700-001-F00
(2) Do this check of the blocker door:
NOTE: If there is side movement of the blocker door or if more than three threads show at the
end of the bolt at the clamped hinge, this is an indication that the hinge is not clamped.
(a) Make sure that there is no side movement of the blocker door at the hinges.
(b) Make sure that no more than three threads show at the end of the bolts [11].
1) If there is side movement of the blocker door at the hinges, or more than three
threads show at the end of the bolt, add more washers [13] at the nut [14].
2) Tighten the nut [14] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 78-31-06-410-003-F00
(3) Do these steps to connect the drag link [4] to the blocker door [1] (door 1 and 6), blocker
door [2] (door 2-4 and 7-9), or blocker door [3] (door 5 and 10) (View C, Figure 401):
(a) Remove Vibration Damping T ape 434 tape, G02329, that holds the drag link against the
inner wall of the fan duct.
(b) Make sure that there is a protective mat, STD-585, in the fan duct.
(c) Remove the tie strap that is installed through the spherical bearing to hold the ball in its
position.
(d) Align the drag link [4] and control link attach holes.
(e) Install the bolt [8], bushing [16], washer [6], washer [7], and nut [5].
1) Tighten the nut [5] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 240 in-lb (27.1 N·m).
(f) Remove the protective mat, STD-585, and cotton wiper, G00034.
78-31-06
SUBTASK 78-31-06-410-005-F00
WARNING
OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE PROCEDURE TO CLOSE THE THRUST
REVERSERS, BUT DO NOT DO THE THRUST REVERSER OR LEADING
EDGE ACTIVATION. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURIES
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(4) Close and latch the thrust reverser but do not do the thrust reverser or leading edge activation
and do not close the fan cowl panels at this time (TASK 78-31-00-010-804-F00).
(a) Remove the short thrust reverser lock, SPL-23566, from the extended piston rod.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-980-002-F00
(5) Manually translate the sleeve through an extend and retract cycle.
(a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-803-F00.
(b) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Manual Procedure),
TASK 78-31-00-980-804-F00.
1) Make sure that the blocker doors and drag links move smoothly.

(1) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Activation After Ground Maintenance,

SUBTASK 78-31-06-710-001-F00
(2) Operate the thrust reverser a minimum of three cycles:
(a) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Power Procedure),

(b) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Power Procedure),

E. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 78-31-06-010-001-F00
WARNING
OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THIS PROCEDURE WHEN YOU OPEN THE
THRUST REVERSERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS,
INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
F . Procedure
SUBTASK 78-31-06-210-001-F00
(1) Look for missing blocker doors.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-900-001-F00
(2) If you find missing blocker doors, replace the blocker doors.
These are the tasks:
(a) Blocker Door Removal, TASK 78-31-06-000-801-F00.
(b) Blocker Door Installation, TASK 78-31-06-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-210-002-F00
(3) Examine the blocker doors for the damage that follows:
NOTE: Refer to SRM 54–30–01 for allowable damage limits.
(a) Holes
Cracks
Nicks
Gouges
Scratches
Dents
Edge Damage
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPOSITE BLOCKER DOORS
Delamination
1) If you find damage, replace the blocker door.
a) Blocker Door Removal, TASK 78-31-06-000-801-F00
b) Blocker Door Installation, TASK 78-31-06-400-801-F00.
NOTE: Composite blocker doors may be repaired in accordance with SRM
54–30–01 and returned to service.
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ALUMINUM BLOCKER DOORS
2) If you find damage, refer to SRM 54-30-90 for allowable damage limits and repair
procedures.
RYR ALL
SUBTASK 78-31-06-860-002-F00
(4) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Extend (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-980-801-F00.
78-31-06
SUBTASK 78-31-06-210-004-F00
(5) Visually examine the aft surface of each blocker door for missing wear pads.
NOTE: It may be necessary to use a mirror to see all areas.
NOTE: Blocker doors, P/N 315A2510-9 and -10, 315A2512-15 and -17, and 315A2512-16
and -18, 315A2535-1 and -2, 315A2535-3 and -4, 315A2533-1 do not have wear pads
on the blocker door.
NOTE: Check the part number of the blocker door before installation of a wear pad that
appears to be missing. Blocker doors without wear pads can look almost the same as
blocker doors with missing wear pads.
(a) If you find a wear pad missing, do the steps that follow:
NOTE: Wear pad replacement requires removal of the blocker door.
1) Make a record of each location where a wear pad is missing.
2) For each affected blocker door location, do this task: Blocker Door Removal,
TASK 78-31-06-000-801-F00.
3) If the wear pad is partially installed or is loose, remove it from the blocker door.
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPOSITE BLOCKER DOORS
NOTE: Wear pad removal can cause delamination of the blocker door.
RYR ALL
a) Remove the worn or damage wear pad from the bond assembly.
4) Visually check the blocker door for delamination at the wear pad location.
a) If you find delamination, replace the blocker door.
5) Install the wear pad to the blocker door:
a) Lightly abrade the mating surfaces of the wear pad and the blocker door with
180 grit abrasive paper, G50381 to remove gloss and any contaminants.
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH COMPOSITE BLOCKER DOORS
NOTE: Do not abrade into fibers.
RYR ALL
b) Clean with alcohol, B50073 or alcohol, B00065.
c) Apply adhesive, A01054 to the wear pad.
NOTE: The adhesive, A01054 is the preferred adhesive for in-service
replacement of the wear pad. The adhesive, A01085 is the alternate
adhesive.
<1> Make sure bondline thickness is 0.003-0.010 inches.
<2> Make sure a fillet of adhesive extends out around the part after squeeze
out.
d) Let the adhesive cure.
e) Apply primer, C00766 to surfaces not covered with primer, support or
adhesive.
6) For each affected blocker door location, do this task: Blocker Door Installation,
TASK 78-31-06-400-801-F00.
78-31-06
SUBTASK 78-31-06-210-003-F00
(6) Examine the blocker door support assemblies:
NOTE: The blocker door support assemblies are the two bumpers that are attached to the
translating sleeve below the edge of the each blocker door.
(a) If one support assembly is missing below a blocker door, then the Continue-In-Service
limit is a maximum of 14 days.
NOTE: The limit of 14 days is an action to prevent damage. The limit makes it necessary
for the replacement of the first missing support because it is possible that the
second support could also become detached. Two blocker door supports prevent
the vibration of the closed blocker door. One blocker door support is permitted
because the door is supported. If the second support were to also become
detached, the blocker door will vibrate which will cause wear and damage to the
blocker door and the thrust reverser sleeve.
(b) If two support assemblies are missing below a blocker door, then replace the support
assemblies (TASK 78-31-01-960-803-F00).
NOTE: Continued operation, for a maximum of 14 days, is permitted if one support
assembly is re-installed. If a new part is not available, one support assembly from
an adjacent door, that has two support assemblies, can be removed and
installed.
SUBTASK 78-31-06-860-003-F00
(7) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Operation - Retract (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-980-802-F00.
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
